newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine still sees beet crop flat at 24 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine still sees beet crop flat at 24 mln T.

text.p: Ukraine still expects to produce a sugar beet crop of 24 million tonnes, the same as in 1996, the first deputy agriculture minister said on Thursday.
"We have sown 1.2 million hectares to sugar beets and we estimate we will get 20 tonnes per hectare," Boris Supikhanov told Reuters. "That means around 24 million tonnes of sugar beets this year."
Supikhanov said the figure would remain the same because Ukraine was trying to rein in surplus sugar production.

Agriculture Minister Mykhailo Zubets, also a deputy prime minister in charge of agriculture, last month announced measures effective September 1 to limit sugar sales on the local market to 1.5 million tonnes, which is the amount consumed domestically each year.
He said Ukraine would sell the rest of its sugar abroad.
Russia is a big customer, but has complained that Ukraine is dumping its product at below-market prices.
Ukrainian government forecasts of refined sugar output for this year are unchanged at 3.26 million tonnes -- the same as in 1996 -- after 3.49 million in 1995.
